November 1826'; Saxe-Altenburg page: 'Altenburg to the Duke of Saxe-Hildburghausen, who in exchange gave up Hildburghausen to the Duke of Saxe-Meiningen', after the Gotha line died out in 1825. The Sachsen-Altenburg page names the Ostkreis (Altenburg, Schmölln, Gößnitz, Lucka, Meuselwitz, Ronneburg) and Westkreis (Eisenberg, Kahla, Orlamünde, Roda); the radii are the researcher's reading.

ledger.note: November 1918: the duchy ends in the German Revolution. Infobox 'German Revolution: November 1918' (no day); 'This family ruled the duchy until the end of the monarchies in the course of the German Revolution of 1918-19'; 'The succeeding Free State of Saxe-Altenburg became part of the new State of Thuringia when it formed in 1920.' Infobox status 'State of the German Empire' (no dates on the page). Federal state of the German Empire from 1871 ('The other states retained their own governments but had only limited aspects of sovereignty', German Empire page). Was a dissolve in 1871 into german-empire; moved to November 1918 and the counterpart changed to weimar-republic on the 3 Nov 2026 fix (fx-53 D01, as fx-46 R122 did for Bavaria): the Empire was this state's overlord, not its successor.

certainty.note: A small state with administrative boundaries and exclaves (the Sachsen-Altenburg page names Mumsdorf, Roschütz, Hilbersdorf, Neukirchen, Rußdorf and Ammelstädt); the grid outline cannot draw them. 1872-1918 (fx-53): the dossier records no frontier change after 1871; the state keeps its 1870 outline as a federal state of the German Empire.

notes:
WHICH STATE? Cliopatria's 'Saxe-Altenburg' row (1806-1870) is two things: 1806-1825 the Duchy of Saxe-Gotha-Altenburg (3,007 km2 in 1800), which duchy-of-saxe-gotha-altenburg (batch eu-09-x) already carries to 1826 with a 1735-1825 keyframe, and 1826-1870 a shape that is not Altenburg at all (the cells of Gotha, Eisenberg and Eisenach, no Altenburg cell; the 1836-1839 shape duplicates the combined Gotha-Altenburg outline of 1820-1827, in years Cliopatria also draws Saxe-Coburg and Gotha). This dossier is therefore the Duchy of Saxe-Altenburg from the 1826 division only, reviews the 1806-1825 shapes as 'wrong' (they belong to the Gotha-Altenburg dossier) and replaces the later ones with the Ostkreis/Westkreis radii. That settles the question the Gotha-Altenburg dossier left to the reviewer.

END YEAR 1871 follows the sibling German-state dossiers (the German Empire row takes over); the duchy existed to 13 November 1918.

NOT SETTLED. (1) No page opened dates any Altenburg border change after 1826 (no exchange with Reuss, Schwarzburg, Prussia or Saxony is described); the Saxe-Altenburg page's infobox gives 1826 for the restoration and the Sachsen-Altenburg page 12 November 1826. (2) The 1848 events, the 1831 constitution (29 April 1831), the 1833/34 Zollverein and the 1866/67 North German Confederation are not territorial and are not ledger events. (3) Wars: none of the pages opened mentions one; the Austro-Prussian War of 1866 and the 4 February 1867 military convention with Prussia (Sachsen-Altenburg page) are not treated. (4) The cells of Eisenberg/Kahla in the Westkreis are approximate.

GAZETTEER NAMES WANTED (the radii use coordinates): Altenburg 12.44E 50.99N, Eisenberg (Thuringia) 11.90E 50.97N, Roda/Stadtroda and Kahla 11.64E 50.82N.

COUNTERPARTS NEEDING DOSSIERS: Saxe-Hildburghausen (1680-1826), Saxe-Meiningen before 1820 (the Hildburghausen exchange). REALM OF MEMBER STATES (fx-53 D01, 3 Nov 2026): this state now lives to November 1918 as a federal state of the German Empire, which 'retained their own governments' (German Empire page: 'The other states retained their own governments but had only limited aspects of sovereignty'; 'the Kaiser and all German ruling kings, dukes, and princes abdicated' in November 1918) and the German revolution of 1918-1919 page: 'By the end of the month, the dynastic rulers of all the other German states had abdicated without bloodshed'. Changed: identity.end 1871 -> 1918/11; the 1871 dissolve into german-empire became a 1918/11 dissolve into weimar-republic; successors german-empire -> weimar-republic; last keyframe (saxe-altenburg_1870) carried to 1918 ('to'); capital and certainty to 1918. The german-empire dossier no longer gains this land in 1871 nor lists the state as a predecessor, and weimar-republic lists it as a predecessor (fx-53 D02, D04). The hierarchy.csv row saxe-altenburg -> german-empire (constituent, 1871-1918) is for the orchestrator. The Saxe-Altenburg page gives 'November 1918' without a day.
